problem:
Compute the variance ${\sigma }^{2}$ of the following data set:

$$
10,\,23,\,17,\,18
$$

${\sigma }^{2}=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance of the data set is given by 

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ is the mean of the data set.

First, we need to compute the mean. There are $n=4$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (10+23+17+18) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 68 \\  & =17.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(10-17)^{2}+(23-17)^{2}+(17-17)^{2}+(18-17)^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[49+36+0+1] \\  & =\frac{86}{4} \\  & =21.5.\end{aligned}
$$
